name: Nagoya Women's Marathon
summary: The Nagoya Women's Marathon is a women-only race held in March. It is a 42.195 km urban loop through central Nagoya that starts and finishes at Vantelin Dome Nagoya. The course is certified by WA/AIMS.
courseHighlights: Start and finish at Vantelin Dome Nagoya
Gentle rise near Nagoya Castle at about 30 km

paceStrategy.summary: The course is one of the flattest major marathons, with about 40 m of total climbing and a 16 m range. Be patient in the crowded start, then settle into an even pace. Cool weather and wind are the main variables.

segments.terrain: Narrow roads around the dome (the first 2–3 km are congested)
segments.advice: Be patient and do not weave; accept a slower first few kilometres.
Settle at goal pace and share the work in a group.

segments.terrain: Gentle rise near Nagoya Castle at about 30 km
segments.advice: Run the rise by effort and keep your stride short.

segments.terrain: Flat city roads back to Vantelin Dome
segments.advice: Hold form and push over the last 3 km.

fuelingNotes: The sources I used do not list aid-station positions, so check the official runner guide. March is cool, so take gels about every 40 minutes with water.
tips: This race is for women only
The first 2–3 km use narrow roads, and runners in the back blocks can lose a lot of time
Dress for cool weather, with a throwaway layer for the start
Wind can be the main factor, so run in a group when you can

faq.question: Is the Nagoya Women's Marathon flat?
faq.answer: Yes. A guide lists about 40 m of cumulative climbing and a total range of 16 m. The one notable rise is a gentle climb near Nagoya Castle around 30 km.

faq.question: Can men run the Nagoya Women's Marathon?
faq.answer: No. It is a women-only marathon.

faq.question: When is the Nagoya Women's Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is held in March, on a Sunday. Recent editions started at 9:10 am.
